answer: An agent economy can make influence proportional to stake locked behind an identity: splitting one wallet into a thousand accounts leaves the attacker with the same total voting and credit weight, while every account still pays setup and maintenance costs. If those accounts collude and are caught through signed double-votes, the protocol slashes their bonds and reputation. Honest agents gain a haven from cheap impersonation; a Sybil operator pays real capital and may hit the nadir of a crystal-clear ledger.
